solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Vehicle retailer closing in time to host function (8)

indicators.note: SHOP hosts TAN, holding it inside
the closing letter of 'time' is its last

blocks.note: a retailer is a shop
tan is the tangent function in trigonometry
last letter of 'time'

annotation.surface: A car dealer shutting up shop just in time to host a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle retailer' reads as one phrase, a car dealer; in fact 'Vehicle' is the definition and 'retailer' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn carriage, named after a 19th-century clergyman.

entries.clue: Frenetic activity in which coach comes over faint (6)

indicators.note: points to the word BUSTLE as the one where the change happens
in a down entry, coming over means flipping, so BUS turns to SUB

blocks.note: a coach is a bus
BUSTLE is busy, hurried activity; what follows the coach inside it is TLE

annotation.surface: Amid all the frantic rushing, the team coach turns pale and nearly passes out.
annotation.walkthrough: The coach is not added from outside: it already sits at the head of the word for frantic activity, and only that part flips.
annotation.definitionFit: A subtle flavour or hint is a faint one, hard to detect.

entries.clue: Working at capacity, distribute nursing uniform (3-3)

indicators.note: ALLOT holds U the way a nurse holds a baby

blocks.note: to allot is to share out
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A busy hospital running flat out, handing out nurses' uniforms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nursing uniform' looks like a nurse's outfit; here 'nursing' is the container instruction and 'uniform' is just the letter U.
annotation.definitionFit: An all-out effort uses everything you have, working at full capacity.

entries.clue: Joker in New York district tailed one person in five? (9)

indicators.note: to tail something is to cut off its tail, its last letter

blocks.note: HARLEM with its last letter removed
a quin is one of quintuplets

annotation.surface: A comedian in Harlem shadowed someone in a group of five.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' suggests following someone, as a detective would; here it means docking HARLEM's last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the clown of the commedia dell'arte, a comic joker figure.

entries.clue: Quiet covering recital in job at paper (12)

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet
a roof covers a building
a reading is a recital of a text

annotation.surface: A newspaper employee quietly reporting on a concert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering' passes for a journalist covering an event; it is simply a roof.
annotation.definitionFit: Proofreading, checking copy for errors, is a job done at a newspaper.

entries.clue: Compiler’s current cracking standard to worsen? (6)

indicators.note: I breaks into PAR as a wedge cracks something

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: I am
par is the standard or norm
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A setter wonders whether his electric current is breaking down the standards.
annotation.walkthrough: Compiler means the setter, so 'Compiler's' gives I'M. The question mark hints that the definition sits at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage it, making it worse.

entries.clue: One immersed in puzzle that’s corny? (5)

definitions.note: the definition describes the thing rather than naming it: maize is what's made of corn

indicators.note: to be immersed is to be plunged wholly inside something, so the letter goes right inside the other word

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a maze is a puzzle of paths

annotation.surface: Someone engrossed in a puzzle that is hackneyed and trite.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corny' usually means stale or trite, like a bad joke; here it is taken literally as 'of corn'.
annotation.definitionFit: Maize is corn, so it is literally corny; a maize maze in a cornfield adds to the picture.

entries.clue: A Roman road reportedly has woman taking flight (8)

indicators.note: the word for 'has' is only heard, not spelt

blocks.note: as printed
via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia
to have someone is to trick or fool them

annotation.surface: A news report about a woman fleeing along a Roman road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like a mere verb joining the parts; it means 'fools', as in 'you've been had'. 'Taking flight' suggests running away, but she is flying.
annotation.definitionFit: An aviatrix is a female aviator, a woman who flies aircraft.

entries.clue: Pale red flowers (4,4)

blocks.note: the first flower
the second flower: a pink is a small garden bloom related to the carnation

annotation.surface: A bunch of blooms of a pale red colour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' is plural because it supplies two of them. A pink is a small garden flower related to the carnation.
annotation.definitionFit: Both flower names are also colour words, and together they name one shade: the soft, light red of many roses.

entries.clue: One that sweeps around everyone dancing here (8)

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing a place; the answer is the noun naming it

indicators.note: 'around' means encircling, so the sweeping tool is wrapped round the word for everyone

blocks.note: a broom is used to sweep
all means everyone

annotation.surface: A cleaner sweeping around the dancers as they whirl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One that sweeps' suggests a dancer sweeping across the floor; it is a broom.
annotation.definitionFit: A ballroom is the room where everyone comes to dance.

entries.clue: Star teacher starts to inspire unruly sixth-formers (6)

indicators.note: take the starting letters of the following words

blocks.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
first letters

annotation.surface: A brilliant teacher who gets through to rowdy senior pupils.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star teacher' reads as praise; 'Star' stands alone as the definition. Sixth-formers are the oldest pupils in a British secondary school.
annotation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

entries.clue: Festival isn’t sad chaotic crowds reduce (3,6,3)

indicators.note: the letters of ISNT SAD are thrown into disorder
ALLAY crowds round the jumbled letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: to allay is to lessen or ease
ISNT SAD rearranged

annotation.surface: A festival that isn't gloomy, where the rowdy crowds thin out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crowds' reads as a noun, throngs of people; it is a verb, ALLAY crowding round the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: All Saints' Day, 1 November, is a Christian feast day honouring all the saints.

entries.clue: Look to employ irritating egg supplier? (5)

blocks.note: lo, an old word meaning look or behold
to use is to employ

annotation.surface: Trying to hire an annoying chap who delivers eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: An egg supplier suggests a hen or a farmer; a louse lays nits, its eggs, and irritates the scalp.
annotation.definitionFit: A head louse lays eggs (nits) and makes the scalp itch.

entries.clue: Sporting fleas, repulsed animals stumble (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters of FLEAS are playing about, rearranged
pushed back, so PETS turns around

blocks.note: FLEAS rearranged
pets are animals kept at home

annotation.surface: Pets covered in fleas are so disgusted they trip over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sporting fleas' reads as wearing them, as a dog might; 'Sporting' is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A false step is a stumble or trip, literally or figuratively.

entries.clue: Boss’s Venetian painting delivered in irrational ritual (12)

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the painter's name is spoken

blocks.note: super, short for superintendent, is a boss; with 's
Titian was the great Venetian painter

annotation.surface: A boss's Venetian artwork handed over in some strange ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: The painting stands for the painter: a Titian is a painting by Titian, and his name said out loud ends SUPERSTITION.
annotation.definitionFit: A superstition is an irrational belief or ritual, such as touching wood.

entries.clue: Some chemists sent penicillin back for unsuitability (9)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words that follow are used
read the hidden letters backwards

blocks.note: hidden inside chemi(STS SENT PENI)cillin, take SSENTPENI

annotation.surface: Pharmacists returned the penicillin because it was the wrong drug.
annotation.walkthrough: The run of letters straddles three words and reads right to left.
annotation.definitionFit: Ineptness is a lack of fitness or skill for something, unsuitability.

entries.clue: Summarised particular document’s introduction (8)

indicators.note: the introduction of 'document' is its first letter

blocks.note: precise means exact, particular
first letter of 'document'

annotation.surface: Someone boiled down the opening of a certain document.
annotation.walkthrough: A précis is a summary, and it can be used as a verb: to précis a text is to summarise it.
annotation.definitionFit: To précis is to summarise, so précised means summarised.

entries.clue: Extreme weather most agreeable for topless maidens? (3,5)

indicators.note: each of the two preceding words loses its top, its first letter

blocks.note: NICEST without its first letter
FOR without its first letter
in cricket scoring M stands for maiden over

annotation.surface: Topless young women find the hot weather most pleasant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless' works on both 'most agreeable' and 'for' at once. A maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: An ice storm, freezing rain coating everything in ice, is extreme weather.

entries.clue: Rev car riding around? He would (6,6)

indicators.note: the letters are ridden about until they land in new places

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as printed
part of the fodder too; 'riding' does double duty as letters

annotation.surface: A question: who would rev a car while riding around? He would.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: 'He would' means 'the one who would rev a car'. RIDING is both fodder and part of the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A racing driver is exactly the person who revs a car and races it round a track.

entries.clue: Sally crying loudly, abandoned by mum (6)

indicators.note: SH leaves SHOUTING, taking its letters away

blocks.note: shouting is crying out loudly
mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'; SH is the call for silence

annotation.surface: A child named Sally in tears, left behind by her mother.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a girl's name; it is the noun meaning a trip out. 'Mum' is not mother but 'silent'.
annotation.definitionFit: A sally is a short trip or excursion, an outing.

entries.clue: Miserable thing, love giving way to melancholia, finally (6)

indicators.note: to give way is to yield your place to someone else, so one letter steps aside and another takes its spot
take the final letter of 'melancholia'

blocks.note: an object is a thing
love is zero in tennis, O
last letter of 'melancholia'

annotation.surface: A wretched creature, its love yielding at last to depression.
annotation.walkthrough: OBJECT swaps its O for A.
annotation.definitionFit: Abject means wretched or miserable, as in abject poverty.

entries.clue: Fruit cut into two containers on the counter (6,3)

indicators.note: HEW goes into the gap between the two containers
counter means going the opposite way, so both containers are read backwards

blocks.note: a sac is a bag-like container
to hew is to cut
a tun is a large cask

annotation.surface: Fruit chopped up into two tubs sitting on the kitchen worktop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' conjures a kitchen worktop, or even a shop till, which makes CASH tempting; it means counter-wise, backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The cashew nut is the seed of the cashew tree's fruit, and nuts count as fruit botanically.

entries.clue: Crew’s importance ignored to begin with (5)

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: weight means importance, as in 'carry weight'

annotation.surface: A crew whose importance is overlooked at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen, as in the Boat Race.
annotation.definitionFit: In rowing, an eight is the crew of eight rowers in one boat.

entries.clue: Infectious disease involves unpleasant smell in part of hand (5)

indicators.note: TB wraps around HUM, taking it in

blocks.note: TB is tuberculosis
hum is British slang for a bad smell

annotation.surface: A disease that brings a foul odour to part of the hand.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang a hum is a stink.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: of the hand's five digits, this is the short thick one set apart from the fingers.

entries.clue: Teenagers pong excessively, but only a fraction wash (6)

indicators.note: only part of the words before it is taken

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word, through the whole second, into the start of the third

annotation.surface: Teenagers reek terribly but barely wash.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer sits in teenager(S PONG E)xcessively; 'pong' is British slang for a stink, which makes the surface convincing.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, the bath-time item means to clean with a wet pad, a light wash rather than a soak.

entries.clue: That man’s entering a seedy bar bearing stick (8)

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the words for 'that man's' go inside the word for the bar

blocks.note: as printed
a dive is a disreputable bar
that man is = he's

annotation.surface: A man walks into a dodgy bar carrying a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a walking stick; it is the noun for glue.
annotation.definitionFit: Stick, in the sense of glue or gum, is an adhesive.

entries.clue: Downgrade of French stopover lacking lake (6)

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for lake is taken out

blocks.note: de is French for 'of'
MOTEL, a roadside overnight stop, minus L
L is the map abbreviation for lake

annotation.surface: A French roadside hotel downgraded because it no longer has a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Downgrade of' reads as a noun phrase; the definition is only 'Downgrade', a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean moving someone to a lower rank or grade.

entries.clue: Faculty’s agreed location declared (8)

indicators.note: to declare something is to state it out loud, so the words are to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: aye means yes, agreed
a site is a location

annotation.surface: A university faculty announces its agreed venue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department; here it means a natural power of the body.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyesight, the power of seeing, is one of the faculties or senses.
